persona.who: 29, chartered accountant in Indore, married 1 year, lives with in-laws who expect her to give up the practice after a baby. Husband avoids the topic.
persona.note: my mother in law keeps saying once the baby comes you will anyway leave all this CA work. I built my practice from zero. my husband just changes the subject. I feel like I am slowly being erased

understanding.bridge: The life they say you will leave after the baby is the one you built from zero, and the Gita says the self that does the work cannot be given away.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being told you will be erased to standing in the truth that cannot be spoken away.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being told you will be erased, and the anger of it, named without blame.

understanding.core_struggle: A woman who built her own CA practice is being told by her mother-in-law she will leave it after the baby, while her husband stays silent.
understanding.mirror: You built this from nothing, and they are already writing the ending before the story begins.
understanding.insight: The practice you built from zero is the most real thing in that room. The sentence they keep repeating is their fear, not your future.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Tension with my in-laws. Being seen as less than you are by the people who ought to know you best, and the anger of watching the life you built get called a phase.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A woman of standing, dismissed by her own husband's family, who questioned them openly and stood in her truth until they had no answer.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, when Arjuna is overwhelmed by grief and doubt. He tells him that you alone must be your own supporter, because you alone can be your own ruin.
verse.for_you: You built this practice from zero. Let that truth stand against the sentence they keep repeating about your future. You do not need their permission to see your own worth.

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Ravana's ministers flatter him as Ram's army arrives; the poet comments.
verse.sanskrit: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥
verse.line: When advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you, the ruin comes quickly.
verse.translation: When a minister, a doctor and a teacher speak only to please, out of fear or hope of reward, then the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed.
verse.why: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

prasang.title: Mandodari pleads, the ministers flatter
prasang.summary: Mandodari takes Ravana aside and begs him to return Sita before it is too late. He laughs at her fear and goes to court, where his ministers tell him only what pleases him. Tulsidas notes that when advisers, doctors and teachers speak only to please, ruin comes quickly.
prasang.story_hook: Mandodari took her husband's hand and led him somewhere the ministers couldn't hear.
prasang.lesson: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

verse.meaning: Tulsidas watches Ravana in his court, surrounded by ministers who flatter him into disaster. He warns that when a circle only echoes what you want to hear, it prepares your undoing.
verse.for_you: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: Rules of conduct for a renunciant.
verse.sanskrit: नात्यर्थं सुखदुःखाभ्यां शरीरमुपतायेत् । स्तूयमानो न तुषेत निन्दितो न शपेत्परान् ॥
verse.line: Don't wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. Praised, don't gloat; blamed, don't curse others.
verse.translation: Let him not torment the body too much for the sake of pleasure or pain. Praised, let him not gloat; blamed, let him not curse others.
verse.meaning: A teacher lays down the rules for a renunciant. He tells the student to let him not torment the body too much for the sake of pleasure or pain. Praised, let him not gloat. Blamed, let him not curse others. The teaching is to hold a steady course through both praise and blame without letting either move your inner balance.
verse.for_you: The self cannot be cut, burned or made less; what they see is a role, and you were never only a role.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated in despair after he has lost his kingdom. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt or settle for too little. She says he must set his mind on what is truly good, stop being afraid, and pull himself together. The idea is that past failure does not define you, and those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha that a person who is truly free moves through the world by doing the work that comes to them, treating friend and foe alike, and letting go of wanting and not-wanting. Such a person speaks gently, reads the intent of others' hearts, and does not sink in the world. The idea is to live fully in the world while staying unhurried and calm inside.
verse.for_you: The work you built from zero is in front of you right now. Do it, and let the silence from the other room be what it is. You will not sink.

story.title: Janaka's family joins the council
story.story_hook: Sita's parents walked into the forest camp, and two grieving families sat down together.
story.summary: Sita's parents arrive and the two families grieve together. Kausalya tells Sunayana that people, like gold, are proved by time. Janaka asks Bharat to decide, and Bharat declines: duty and self-interest pull apart, hatred is blind and love cannot reason, so he will follow Ram's wish. His few words leave the whole court in awe.
story.lesson: When you are too close to a decision, say so, and speak briefly and honestly.

anchor.speaker: Kausalya
anchor.setting: Kausalya, to Sita's mother at Chitrakoot, on Bharat's character.
anchor.sanskrit: जानउँ सदा भरत कुलदीपा। बार बार मोहि कहेउ महीपा॥ कसें कनकु मनि पारिखि पाएँ। पुरुष परिखिअहिं समयँ सुभाएँ ॥
anchor.line: Gold is proved on the touchstone. People are proved by time.
anchor.translation: I have always known Bharat to be the lamp of our family; the king told me so again and again. Gold is known on the touchstone and a gem when a jeweller comes; a person is tested by time and shows his nature.
anchor.why: When you are too close to a decision, say so, and speak briefly and honestly.

script: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult. Krishna said to Arjuna:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्, आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः.
In plain words: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, when Arjuna is overwhelmed by grief and doubt. He tells him that you alone must be your own supporter, because you alone can be your own ruin.
For you, today. You built this practice from zero. Let that truth stand against the sentence they keep repeating about your future. You do not need their permission to see your own worth.
And what it does not mean. Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

depth.life: Your mother-in-law says you will leave your practice after the baby, and your husband changes the subject. You sit with the phone in your hand, erased and quietly furious, your own CA practice built from zero now feeling fragile.
depth.points: The Gita says the self that does the work cannot be given away. Your mother-in-law speaks a sentence, but it is not your future. The self that built this practice from zero is the only truth that cannot be erased.
depth.practice: When the phone is in your hand, look at your own reflection and say, 'I am my own friend.'
depth.question: What does it feel like to stand on your own side?
